subsystems.name: Target cells
subsystems.role: the cell types that actually determine appearance, once edited.
parts: melanocytes in the basal skin layer (pigment)

subsystems.name: Editing payload
subsystems.role: the molecular tool that rewrites a chosen gene or letter of DNA.
parts: Cas9 nuclease or a base editor that changes one DNA base without cutting
regulatory sequence to switch the gene on in the right cell

subsystems.name: Delivery vehicle
subsystems.role: gets the payload past the skin barrier and into the intended cell type.
parts: engineered viral vectors (e.g. HSV-1 or AAV)

subsystems.name: Specificity control
subsystems.role: keeps the edit in skin, in the right cells, and off every other gene.

subsystems.name: Safety and reversibility
subsystems.role: limits damage if the edit behaves unexpectedly.

subsystems.name: Assessment
subsystems.role: measures the result objectively rather than by eye.

buildSteps.title: Identify the causal genes
buildSteps.detail: Pigment work would start from genes already linked to human colour variation — MC1R, TYR, OCA2 and SLC24A5 — while texture work targets collagen and elastin genes and their regulators.

buildSteps.title: Design the editor
buildSteps.detail: For pigment, a base editor that flips a single DNA letter is safer than a nuclease, which cuts both strands and risks rearrangements; some changes, such as silencing a gene, need the cutting version.

buildSteps.title: Choose a delivery route
buildSteps.detail: Microneedle arrays or lipid nanoparticles would carry the payload a fraction of a millimetre into the epidermis and upper dermis, where melanocytes and fibroblasts sit.

buildSteps.title: Prove it in skin models
buildSteps.detail: Edited cells are grown into reconstituted human skin in the lab and checked for correct pigment or protein production and for unintended edits.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Pig skin is the closest animal model, since its pigmentation and thickness resemble human skin; edits are confined to a marked patch and followed for months.

buildSteps.title: Treat a defined patch
buildSteps.detail: In any first human use, a small area is treated and left to stabilise for a season or more, because melanocyte activity varies with sun exposure and hormones.

buildSteps.title: Measure objectively
buildSteps.detail: Colour is read with a spectrophotometer and the treated skin is biopsied and sequenced to confirm the intended edit and exclude others.

buildSteps.title: Monitor for the long term
buildSteps.detail: Edited skin is checked regularly for uncontrolled growth, since permanently altered cells divide for decades.

prerequisites.tech: Safe in-vivo gene delivery to skin
prerequisites.why: a topical gene therapy for the blistering disorder epidermolysis bullosa was approved in the United States in 2023, showing skin editing is possible but only for a narrow defect.
no current method reliably edits melanocytes while leaving neighbouring keratinocytes and immune cells untouched.
major genes are known, but human skin colour is polygenic and heavily modified by sun, hormones and inflammation, so an edit does not map cleanly to one outcome.

prerequisites.tech: Long-term safety data on somatic editing
prerequisites.why: decades of follow-up are needed before permanent edits to dividing cells can be called routine, especially for a non-medical goal.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory and ethical framework for elective edits
prerequisites.why: rules are built for treating disease, not for altering healthy appearance; heritable (germline) editing is separately and widely prohibited.

pathway.milestone: medical skin gene therapies and pigmentation research
pathway.unlocks: proof that skin cells can be edited safely enough for a clinical benefit.

pathway.milestone: somatic editing for disfiguring pigment loss, such as vitiligo or piebaldism
pathway.unlocks: restoring rather than redesigning appearance, and the safety record that comes with it.

pathway.milestone: localised editing of scarring or skin fragility
pathway.unlocks: demonstration that texture, not just pigment, is addressable.

pathway.milestone: elective aesthetic edits at a chosen site
pathway.unlocks: permanent change without ink, surgery or pigment cells — alongside difficult questions about consent, identity and equity.
